得人以造周是豈無其故哉甞仰觀雲漢而知
其化天下者有道焉象亘東南長竟周天之度
punctuated:
宇宙間，謂非得於訓戒之力哉？此萬世君臣之所當法也。

倬彼雲漢，爲章于天。周王壽考，遐不作人？追琢其章，金玉其相。勉勉我王，綱紀四方。

吳應科

同考試官敎諭何批：善說聖人之心法，且體裁整齊，文詞純雅，殆異乎諸子之撰也。高薦允宜。

考試官敎授韓批：理趣雋永，宜錄之以式多士。

考試官敎授劉批：聖人善敎善政，發明殆盡。錄之。

詩人兩興聖人之德，有以會王道之全焉。夫化以作人，治以統人，王道備矣。非文王之德之盛，其孰能與於斯哉？宜詩人取興而形諸咏歌也。意豈不曰：至渙者人之心，至神者君之德。文王得人以造周，是豈無其故哉？甞仰觀雲漢，而知其化天下者有道焉。象亘東南，長竟周天之度，
translation_en:
…throughout the universe. Could this have been achieved without the power of instruction and admonition? This is what rulers and ministers in all ages ought to emulate.

“Brilliant is that Milky Way, forming a pattern in heaven. Long-lived is the king of Zhou: how could he fail to nurture men? Chiseled and polished is his refinement; gold and jade are his substance. Tirelessly our king orders and regulates the four quarters.”

Wu Yingke.

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: “He explains well the sage’s essential principles of the mind. Moreover, the composition is orderly and balanced, and its language pure and elegant. It stands quite apart from the compositions of the other candidates. A high recommendation is entirely fitting.”

Comment by Examiner Han, Professor: “Its treatment of principle has a lasting savor. It should be selected as a model for the many scholars.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “The sage’s excellent teaching and excellent governance are elucidated almost exhaustively. Select it.”

Through two evocative comparisons, the poet presents the sage’s virtue, thereby comprehending the kingly Way in its entirety. Through moral transformation, men are nurtured; through governance, men are brought into an ordered whole: thus the kingly Way is complete. Without virtue as abundant as King Wen’s, who could attain this? It is fitting that the poet should draw on evocative comparisons and give them expression in song. Does his meaning not amount to this? Nothing is more prone to dispersion than human hearts; nothing is more wondrously efficacious than a ruler’s virtue. King Wen won men’s allegiance and thereby established Zhou: could this have been without a cause? Looking up at the Milky Way, one comes to understand that there was a Way by which he transformed all under Heaven. Its configuration stretches across the southeast, its length extending through the full circuit of heaven…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
光聯箕斗明垂下濟之章是有至大之體者必
有至明之用矣矧我周王壽考有不作人者乎
蓋聖德固妙於感通亦必積久而後成也今多
歷年所有以膺壽祺之介則至化敷宣鼓其維
新之機也純德涵濡變其比德之習也凡得於
甄陶者若或振其氣而使之奮矣寧有自外於
文教者哉又嘗俯察物理而知其統天下者有
道焉追琢以為文雕飾盡人官之能金玉以為
質純瑩得天成之妙是有制器之精者必有成
===
器之利矣矧我周王之勉勉有不綱紀四方者
乎蓋聖治固神於推行亦惟純心而後達也今
純亦不已宥以持不息之貞則志意之所孚交
範圍之而不過也精神之所運用曲成之而不
遺也凡在其聯屬者若或握其機而繫其心矣
會有自睽於至治者哉夫振作而人迪其教則
師道立矣綱紀而人訓其政則君道立矣君師
道盡天下歸心焉然則髦士六師固囿於政教
之中者其歸於文王也固宜雖然聖人之治本
punctuated: 光聯箕斗，明垂下濟之章，是有至大之體者必有至明之用矣。矧我周王壽考，有不作人者乎？蓋聖德固妙於感通，亦必積久而後成也。今多歷年所，有以膺壽祺之介，則至化敷宣，鼓其維新之機也；純德涵濡，變其比德之習也。凡得於甄陶者，若或振其氣而使之奮矣，寧有自外於文教者哉？又嘗俯察物理，而知其統天下者有道焉。追琢以為文，雕飾盡人官之能；金玉以為質，純瑩得天成之妙。是有制器之精者必有成器之利矣。矧我周王之勉勉，有不綱紀四方者乎？蓋聖治固神於推行，亦惟純心而後達也。今純亦不已，宥以持不息之貞，則志意之所孚，交範圍之而不過也；精神之所運用，曲成之而不遺也。凡在其聯屬者，若或握其機而繫其心矣，會有自睽於至治者哉？夫振作而人迪其教，則師道立矣；綱紀而人訓其政，則君道立矣。君師道盡，天下歸心焉。然則髦士六師，固囿於政教之中者，其歸於文王也固宜。雖然，聖人之治本
translation_en:
…Its radiance links the Winnowing Basket and Dipper constellations; its light displays the pattern of beneficence descending below. Thus, what possesses the greatest substance must possess the most luminous efficacy. How much more so our long-lived king of Zhou: could he fail to nurture men of worth? The virtue of a sage is indeed wondrous in its power to move others and communicate with them, yet its achievement also requires long accumulation. Having now passed through many years and received the aid of blessings of longevity, he spreads his consummate transforming influence, stirring in people the impulse to renew themselves. His pure virtue bathes and nourishes them, changing their habits toward emulation of virtue [?]. All who receive his molding seem to have their vital energies roused and be impelled to exert themselves. Could any exclude themselves from his civilizing instruction?

I have also looked down and examined the principles of things, and thereby understood that there is a Way by which he unites all under Heaven. Chiseling and polishing produce ornament, with carving and decoration exhausting the skill of human faculties [?]; gold and jade provide the substance, whose purity and brilliance embody the wonder of natural perfection. Thus, excellence in fashioning a vessel necessarily yields the benefits of the finished vessel. How much more so our tireless king of Zhou: could he fail to order the four quarters? The governance of a sage is indeed marvelous in its execution, yet only through purity of heart can it reach everywhere. Now his purity likewise never ceases, sustaining [?] an unremitting constancy. Wherever his intentions inspire trust, he comprehensively encompasses and regulates people so that they do not transgress; wherever his spiritual energies operate, he brings each thing to fulfillment according to its particular circumstances, leaving nothing out. All bound together under him seem to have the springs of their action held and their hearts attached to him. Could any ever estrange themselves from consummate governance?

By rousing people so that they follow his instruction, he establishes the Way of the teacher; by ordering them so that they heed his government, he establishes the Way of the ruler. When the Ways of ruler and teacher are fully realized, all under Heaven turn their hearts to him. Thus, the eminent officers and the six armies are naturally embraced within his government and instruction: it is surely fitting that they should give their allegiance to King Wen. Nevertheless, the governance of a sage is rooted…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
於德而其脩德本於敬然則文王壽考之所感
化勉勉之所致力者固不外於敬止之一言也
其格天心以此其孚人心亦以此厥後武王成
王守為家法用集大統而永天眷焉故知敬者
為帝王傳心之要
春秋
秋九月齊侯宋公江人黃人盟于貫〔僖公二年〕
張炳之
===
同考試官教授林批〔齊桓績在制楚此作能得春秋予之之意〕
考試官教授韓批〔說出聖人予齊之意宜錄〕
考試官教授劉批〔莊重整飭是作春秋者〕
霸主結遠以攘外春秋深予之焉此見齊桓之
服楚慮周義著在此盟也春秋予之無非為世
道計與貫澤曷盟乎齊桓服江黃也夫楚雖大
邦齊未有以膺之而徒結爾與國春秋何予之
深耶蓋中國之不獲寧者以荆楚為之梗也不
punctuated:
於德，而其脩德本於敬。然則文王壽考之所感化、勉勉之所致力者，固不外於敬止之一言也。其格天心以此，其孚人心亦以此。厥後武王、成王守為家法，用集大統而永天眷焉。故知敬者，為帝王傳心之要。
春秋
秋九月，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫。〔僖公二年〕
張炳之
同考試官教授林批〔齊桓績在制楚，此作能得春秋予之之意。〕
考試官教授韓批〔說出聖人予齊之意，宜錄。〕
考試官教授劉批〔莊重整飭，是作春秋者。〕
霸主結遠以攘外，春秋深予之焉。此見齊桓之服楚，慮周義著，在此盟也。春秋予之，無非為世道計與？貫澤曷盟乎？齊桓服江黃也。夫楚雖大邦，齊未有以膺之，而徒結爾與國，春秋何予之深耶？蓋中國之不獲寧者，以荆楚為之梗也。不
translation_en:
…in virtue, while his cultivation of virtue was rooted in reverence. Thus, the influence King Wen exerted throughout his long life, and the tireless efforts to which he devoted himself, amounted to nothing beyond the single injunction to abide in reverence. Through this he moved Heaven’s heart; through this he also won the trust of human hearts. Thereafter, King Wu and King Cheng preserved it as their house’s guiding rule, thereby consolidating the great succession and perpetuating Heaven’s favor. Hence we know that reverence is the essential teaching transmitted from heart to heart among emperors and kings.

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In autumn, in the ninth month, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and men of Jiang and Huang made a covenant at Guan.” 〔Second year of Duke Xi.〕

Zhang Bingzhi

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: 〔Duke Huan of Qi’s achievement lay in checking Chu. This composition grasps the Spring and Autumn Annals’ intention in approving him.〕

Comment by Examiner Han, Instructor: 〔It brings out the sage’s intention in approving Qi. It merits inclusion.〕

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔Dignified and well ordered: this is the work of one who can write on the Spring and Autumn Annals.〕

The hegemon allied with distant states to repel external threats, and the Spring and Autumn Annals accords him profound approval. This covenant reveals the comprehensive planning and manifest righteousness with which Duke Huan of Qi brought Chu into submission. Was not the approval accorded him by the Spring and Autumn Annals entirely out of concern for the order of the world? Why was a covenant made at Guanze? Duke Huan of Qi was bringing Jiang and Huang into allegiance. Now, although Chu was a great state, Qi had yet to find a means of confronting it and merely formed alliances with those other states. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals approve him so deeply? The central states could find no peace because Jing-Chu obstructed them. Unless…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
制乎楚何以免民左袵之憂楚之未來服者以
與國爲之翼也不結江黃無以孤其外助之勢
故桓公不憂夫有楚也而江黃之不吾與是可
憂也不患不能服楚也而其黨之不能攜所深
患也於是約誓以申其詞用合諸侯之衆江黃
自遠而定盟焉夫江黃旣盟則楚勢自孤於東
方矣招徠以攜其黨預圖制楚之計遠國自外
爲掎角焉夫掎角有賴則齊威益震於江漢矣
是兵雖未舉也然剪楚羽翼萬全之謀已臧由
===
是而振旅陘亭由是而來盟召陵孰謂帖服荆
楚之慮不周於今日哉患雖未却也然制敵腹
背折衝之形已定自是而荆蠻是懲自是而周
室始尊孰謂免民左袵之義不著於此盟哉嗚
呼武王牧野之師盛矣猶誓友邦遠及八國焉
豈以齊桓之遠締江黃而非爲攘夷安夏計耶
貫之盟誠霸業之一大機也顧可少乎哉諸侯
皆在獨言遠國者聖人許是盟也經世者可以
思矣抑齊之霸也仲之功也其屈楚也江黃之
punctuated: 制乎楚，何以免民左袵之憂？楚之未來服者，以與國爲之翼也。不結江黃，無以孤其外助之勢。故桓公不憂夫有楚也，而江黃之不吾與是可憂也；不患不能服楚也，而其黨之不能攜所深患也。於是約誓以申其詞，用合諸侯之衆，江黃自遠而定盟焉。夫江黃旣盟，則楚勢自孤於東方矣。招徠以攜其黨，預圖制楚之計，遠國自外爲掎角焉。夫掎角有賴，則齊威益震於江漢矣。是兵雖未舉也，然剪楚羽翼，萬全之謀已臧。由是而振旅陘亭，由是而來盟召陵，孰謂帖服荆楚之慮不周於今日哉？患雖未却也，然制敵腹背，折衝之形已定。自是而荆蠻是懲，自是而周室始尊，孰謂免民左袵之義不著於此盟哉？嗚呼！武王牧野之師盛矣，猶誓友邦，遠及八國焉。豈以齊桓之遠締江黃，而非爲攘夷安夏計耶？貫之盟，誠霸業之一大機也，顧可少乎哉？諸侯皆在，獨言遠國者，聖人許是盟也。經世者可以思矣。抑齊之霸也，仲之功也；其屈楚也，江黃之
translation_en:
…bring Chu under control, how could the people be spared the fear of having to fasten their robes on the left, in the manner of the barbarians? That Chu had not yet submitted was because allied states served as its wings. Without forming ties with Jiang and Huang, there was no way to isolate Chu from its external support. Thus Duke Huan was not worried by Chu’s existence; what worried him was that Jiang and Huang might not join him. He did not fear that he could not subdue Chu; his deepest concern was that he might not detach its allies. Accordingly, he reaffirmed his declarations through pledges and oaths, bringing together the forces of the regional lords, and Jiang and Huang came from afar to conclude the covenant. Once Jiang and Huang had entered the covenant, Chu’s position in the east was naturally isolated. By drawing them over and detaching Chu’s allies, he planned in advance how to bring Chu under control; these distant states would provide coordinated support from outside. With such support to rely upon, Qi’s might resounded still more powerfully throughout the Jiang and Han region. Although troops had not yet been raised, the comprehensive plan to clip Chu’s wings was already sound. This led to the deployment of troops at Xingting and to the conclusion of the covenant at Shaoling. Who could say that the planning for bringing Jing-Chu into submission was not already thorough on this day? Although the danger had not yet been removed, the strategic disposition for controlling the enemy front and rear and checking its assaults was already established. From this followed the chastisement of the barbarians of Jing and the restoration of honor to the royal house of Zhou. Who could say that the righteous purpose of sparing the people from having to fasten their robes on the left was not manifest in this covenant?

Ah! Mighty indeed was King Wu’s army at Muye, yet he still administered an oath to friendly states, reaching as far as the eight states. Could Duke Huan of Qi’s establishment of ties with distant Jiang and Huang, then, be anything other than a plan to repel the barbarians and secure the Xia realm? The covenant at Guan was truly a major turning point in his achievement of hegemony. Could it possibly be regarded as insignificant? The regional lords were all present, yet the text mentions only the distant states: this shows the Sage’s approval of this covenant. Those concerned with ordering the world may reflect upon this. Yet Qi’s hegemony was Guan Zhong’s achievement; its subjugation of Chu was due to Jiang and Huang’s…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
力也齊資其力而不能免其難所負多矣盟貫
之日管仲蓋逆知江黃之必受禍料齊不能救
之非謂齊服楚可無資於江黃也而幸其言之
驗要之始勤終溢霸事靡常君子曰江黃之滅
不在執濤塗之後矣
九月晉侯宋公衛侯鄭伯曹伯會于扈晉
荀林父帥師伐陳〔宣公九年〕
古尚友
同考試官教授林批晉之有禮陳之棄義斷案甚
===
明且行文齊整可錄
考試官教授韓批嚴整
考試官教授劉批渾融傳意成文宜冠本房
春秋紀兵好有予夫近禮者有罪夫棄義者此
見晉之得於討陳而陳之失於從楚也宜春秋
以禮義而示予奪與扈之會何晉謀陳也陳靈
不會於是有林父之伐春秋曷為而予晉也蓋
曰霸者之行於諸侯也非無服人之患惟有禮
以綏之之難陳也貳晉事楚信有罪矣晉苟合
punctuated:
力也。齊資其力而不能免其難，所負多矣。盟貫之日，管仲蓋逆知江黃之必受禍，料齊不能救之，非謂齊服楚可無資於江黃也，而幸其言之驗。要之，始勤終溢，霸事靡常。君子曰：「江黃之滅，不在執濤塗之後矣。」
九月，晉侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯會于扈。晉荀林父帥師伐陳。〔宣公九年〕
古尚友
同考試官教授林批：「晉之有禮，陳之棄義，斷案甚明，且行文齊整，可錄。」
考試官教授韓批：「嚴整。」
考試官教授劉批：「渾融傳意成文，宜冠本房。」
春秋紀兵好，有予夫近禮者，有罪夫棄義者。此見晉之得於討陳，而陳之失於從楚也。宜春秋以禮義而示予奪與！扈之會何？晉謀陳也。陳靈不會，於是有林父之伐。春秋曷為而予晉也？蓋曰：霸者之行於諸侯也，非無服人之患，惟有禮以綏之之難。陳也貳晉事楚，信有罪矣。晉苟合
translation_en:
…their strength. Qi relied on their strength but could not spare them disaster; its debt to them was great indeed. On the day of the covenant at Guan, Guan Zhong presumably foresaw that Jiang and Huang would inevitably suffer calamity and judged that Qi could not rescue them. He did not mean that Qi could subdue Chu without relying on Jiang and Huang, and yet he took satisfaction in the fulfillment of his prediction. In essence, diligence at the outset gave way to excess at the end: the undertaking of a hegemon lacked constancy. The gentleman says: “The destruction of Jiang and Huang was determined even before the arrest of Tao Tu.”
In the ninth month, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, and the Earl of Cao met at Hu. Xun Linfu of Jin led an army to attack Chen. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xuan〕
Gu Shangyou
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Prefectural School Instructor: “The judgment on Jin’s observance of ritual propriety and Chen’s abandonment of righteousness is very clear. The composition is also orderly and well balanced. It merits inclusion.”
Comment by Examiner Han, Prefectural School Instructor: “Rigorous and orderly.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Prefectural School Instructor: “The meaning is conveyed in a fully integrated composition. It should rank first in this examining section.”
In recording warfare and friendly relations [?], the Spring and Autumn Annals approves those who approach ritual propriety and condemns those who abandon righteousness. Here we see that Jin was right to chastise Chen, whereas Chen was wrong to follow Chu. How fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals should use ritual propriety and righteousness to express approval and disapproval! What was the purpose of the meeting at Hu? Jin was planning action against Chen. Duke Ling of Chen did not attend, and so Linfu’s attack followed. Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals approve Jin? It may be said that, in a hegemon’s dealings with the feudal lords, the concern is not simply to make others submit; the difficulty lies in bringing them to peace through ritual propriety. Chen divided its allegiance to Jin and served Chu: it was certainly guilty. If Jin were to assemble…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諸侯之師而兼將往伐未見其力之不濟者顧
戒淫怒而厚自躬匿威武而覬文告必序成不
至而後攻伐始加焉是其先會也徵與同好心
實脩乎詞命繼而伐之也懲其不恪師則利於
執言晉不幾於有禮哉噫因壘之風遠矣春秋
時猶有言招攜以禮如仲父之所以告齊者晉
其近之又曷為而罪陳也蓋曰小國之介于大
國也非徒疆令之從惟有義以裁之之貴晉也
主盟救陳可無與乎陳苟嚴從違之節而矢心
===
===
事晉尤見其防之不潰者顧甘自卑而比匪人
背盟主而附荆夷雖諸侯輯睦以待而竟執迷
弗反焉是扈之會也晉將以懷之也既無以啓
其比從之念而師之伐也晉將以威之也又無
以挽其南向之懷陳不為棄義哉噫商忩之戒
深矣春秋時乃有反覆朝楚如鄭伯之所以貳
晉者陳其蹈之故春秋書林父帥師伐陳於會
扈之下若曰不遽伐而會以待之晉無負於陳
矣會不至而自我致武陳非果於負晉哉此固
punctuated: 諸侯之師而兼將往伐，未見其力之不濟者。顧戒淫怒而厚自躬，匿威武而覬文告，必序成不至而後攻伐始加焉。是其先會也，徵與同好，心實脩乎詞命；繼而伐之也，懲其不恪，師則利於執言。晉不幾於有禮哉？噫！因壘之風遠矣，春秋時猶有言招攜以禮，如仲父之所以告齊者，晉其近之。又曷為而罪陳也？蓋曰：小國之介于大國也，非徒疆令之從，惟有義以裁之之貴。晉也主盟救陳，可無與乎？陳苟嚴從違之節而矢心事晉，尤見其防之不潰者。顧甘自卑而比匪人，背盟主而附荆夷，雖諸侯輯睦以待，而竟執迷弗反焉。是扈之會也，晉將以懷之也，既無以啓其比從之念；而師之伐也，晉將以威之也，又無以挽其南向之懷。陳不為棄義哉？噫！商忩之戒深矣，春秋時乃有反覆朝楚，如鄭伯之所以貳晉者，陳其蹈之。故春秋書林父帥師伐陳於會扈之下，若曰：不遽伐而會以待之，晉無負於陳矣；會不至而自我致武，陳非果於負晉哉？此固
translation_en:
…the armies of the regional lords and jointly lead them against Chen, there would be no reason to suppose its strength inadequate. Yet Jin restrained excessive anger and imposed exacting standards upon itself, withheld its military might and placed its hopes in formal admonitions. Only after the arrangements were completed and Chen failed to appear [?] did it launch an attack. Thus, in first convening the meeting, Jin summoned Chen to share in friendly relations, earnestly attending to diplomatic communications; in subsequently attacking it, Jin punished its lack of respect, its army enjoying the advantage of a justifiable cause. Did Jin not come close to observing ritual propriety? Alas! The tradition of Yinlei [?] was already remote; yet in the Spring and Autumn period there were still those who spoke of winning over the estranged through ritual propriety, as Zhongfu had advised Qi. Jin approached this ideal.

Why, then, does the text condemn Chen? It is saying that a small state situated among great states should not merely obey the commands of the powerful: what matters is judging its course by righteousness. Jin presided over the covenant and had rescued Chen; could Chen refuse to associate with it? Had Chen strictly maintained the principles governing allegiance and refusal, and pledged its heart to serving Jin, its defenses would surely have remained unbroken. Yet it willingly abased itself and associated with unworthy men, turning its back on the leader of the covenant and attaching itself to the barbarians of Jing. Although the regional lords waited for it in concord, it persisted in its delusion and would not turn back. At the meeting at Hu, Jin intended to conciliate it, but this failed to awaken any thought of joining and following Jin. In the military attack, Jin intended to overawe it, but this likewise failed to reverse its inclination toward the south. Was Chen not abandoning righteousness? Alas! The warning of Shangcong [?] was profound; yet in the Spring and Autumn period there were those who shifted their allegiance and paid court to Chu, as the Earl of Zheng did when he wavered in his loyalty to Jin. Chen followed in those footsteps.

Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals records Linfu leading an army to attack Chen immediately after the meeting at Hu. It is as though it says: by convening a meeting and waiting for Chen, instead of attacking at once, Jin did not fail Chen; by failing to attend the meeting and thereby bringing military force upon itself, did Chen not show itself determined to betray Jin? This surely…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖人予晉罪陳意也春秋禮義之大宗此類見
矣抑舉動人君大節也奸邪窺之四鄰視之晉
靈不君宣子專政晉有瑕矣而且歸生徵舒皆
自楚謀之四方諸侯誰不解體陳縱不貳其能
久有之乎悼公復霸內脩外攘駸駸乎二文之
業有餘耀焉君子曰晉君方明八卿和睦蓋異
於靈成時矣
禮記
禮樂皆得謂之有德德者得也
===
馬宗魯
同考試官教諭成 批 發明得禮樂處典實可錄
中式
考試官教授韓 批 是禮樂有得於心者
考試官教授劉 批 造理之文
君子備中和以成德而皆本於心得焉夫中和
會於心斯禮樂有真得矣此君子成德之實下
可以觀知樂之妙乎樂記之意蓋以禮樂本為
合一之理君子自有兼體之能人惟無心得之
punctuated:
聖人予晉罪陳意也。《春秋》禮義之大宗，此類見矣。抑舉動，人君大節也，奸邪窺之，四鄰視之。晉靈不君，宣子專政，晉有瑕矣。而且歸生、徵舒皆自楚謀之，四方諸侯誰不解體？陳縱不貳，其能久有之乎？悼公復霸，內脩外攘，駸駸乎二文之業有餘耀焉。君子曰：「晉君方明，八卿和睦。」蓋異於靈、成時矣。

《禮記》
禮樂皆得，謂之有德。德者，得也。

馬宗魯
同考試官教諭成批：「發明得禮樂處，典實可錄。」中式。
考試官教授韓批：「是禮樂有得於心者。」
考試官教授劉批：「造理之文。」

君子備中和以成德，而皆本於心得焉。夫中和會於心，斯禮樂有真得矣。此君子成德之實，下可以觀知樂之妙乎？《樂記》之意，蓋以禮樂本為合一之理，君子自有兼體之能。人惟無心得之
translation_en:
…the sage’s intention to approve of Jin and condemn Chen. That the Spring and Autumn Annals is the great authoritative source of ritual propriety and righteousness is evident in cases like this. Moreover, a ruler’s conduct is a matter of cardinal importance: the treacherous watch it for opportunities, and neighboring states on every side observe it. Duke Ling of Jin failed to act as a ruler, while Xuanzi monopolized government; Jin thus had its faults. Furthermore, Gui Sheng and Zheng Shu both took their counsel from Chu [?]. Which of the lords throughout the realm would not lose allegiance? Even if Chen had not shifted its allegiance, could Jin have retained it for long? Duke Dao restored Jin’s hegemony, cultivating order within and repelling threats without. His rapid progress lent further luster to the achievements of the two Wen [?]. A gentleman said: “The ruler of Jin is now enlightened, and the eight ministers are harmonious.” This was indeed different from the times of Dukes Ling and Cheng.

Record of Rites
“To attain both ritual and music is called possessing virtue. Virtue means attainment.”

Ma Zonglu
Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor, commented: “His elucidation of what it means to attain ritual and music is grounded in the classics and substantial; it merits selection.” Accepted.
Examiner Han, Professor, commented: “Here is someone who has attained ritual and music in his heart.”
Examiner Liu, Professor, commented: “An essay that penetrates principle.”

The gentleman fully embodies equilibrium and harmony to perfect his virtue, and all of this is rooted in attainment within the heart. When equilibrium and harmony unite in the heart, there is true attainment of ritual and music. This is the substance of the gentleman’s perfected virtue. May we discern from it the subtlety of understanding music [?]? The meaning of the Record of Music is, broadly, that ritual and music are fundamentally a unified principle, and that the gentleman possesses the capacity to embody both. It is only because people lack the subtlety of attainment within the heart…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
妙而始不可以語成德矣君子不惟審音以知
樂也而且能知樂以幾禮焉則聲音寓于倫理
會通於進反之文而中正和樂自兼脩以濟其
美節奏象于事行兼總夫和敬之實而恭敬溫
文自交養以成其行率而循之則交錯於中所
以建中和之極者此也舉而措之則發形於外
所以奮至德之光者此也禮樂皆得而可以謂
之有德矣然是德也豈有待於外哉蓋禮樂非
外至也由心生者也君子之知夫樂也知之以
===
心焉有聲之樂皆無聲者以體其撰樂有真得
而德與樂俱隆矣君子之幾乎禮也幾之以心
焉有體之禮皆無體者以會其精禮有真得而
德與禮俱盛矣夫是之謂禮樂皆得也夫是之
謂有德也而君子知樂之妙觀其深矣抑君子
之於禮樂匪徒得於身心已也擴而充之至禮
不讓而天下治至樂無聲而天下和萬物得其
所焉天地將為昭焉德而至此其盛無以加矣
此中和位育之功體信達順之道
punctuated: 妙，而始不可以語成德矣。君子不惟審音以知樂也，而且能知樂以幾禮焉。則聲音寓于倫理，會通於進反之文，而中正和樂自兼脩以濟其美；節奏象于事行，兼總夫和敬之實，而恭敬溫文自交養以成其行。率而循之，則交錯於中，所以建中和之極者，此也；舉而措之，則發形於外，所以奮至德之光者，此也。禮樂皆得，而可以謂之有德矣。然是德也，豈有待於外哉？蓋禮樂非外至也，由心生者也。君子之知夫樂也，知之以心焉。有聲之樂，皆無聲者以體其撰。樂有真得，而德與樂俱隆矣。君子之幾乎禮也，幾之以心焉。有體之禮，皆無體者以會其精。禮有真得，而德與禮俱盛矣。夫是之謂禮樂皆得也，夫是之謂有德也，而君子知樂之妙，觀其深矣。抑君子之於禮樂，匪徒得於身心已也。擴而充之，至禮不讓而天下治，至樂無聲而天下和，萬物得其所焉，天地將為昭焉。德而至此，其盛無以加矣。此中和位育之功，體信達順之道。
translation_en:
…the subtlety of this, and only then can one no longer speak of completing virtue. The gentleman does not merely discern tones in order to understand music; he can also understand music and thereby approach ritual. Sounds embody the principles of human relationships and find their full expression in the patterned movements of advancing and returning. Thus centrality, correctness, harmony, and joy are cultivated together to perfect their beauty. Rhythms represent deeds and conduct, encompassing the substance of both harmony and reverence. Thus respect, reverence, gentleness, and refinement nourish one another to perfect his conduct. When he follows these principles, they interweave within him: this is how he establishes the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony. When he puts them into practice, they manifest themselves outwardly: this is how he makes the radiance of consummate virtue shine forth. Having attained both ritual and music, he may be called virtuous.

Yet does this virtue depend on anything external? Ritual and music do not arrive from outside; they arise from the heart. When the gentleman understands music, he understands it through his heart. In all music that has sound, that which is soundless embodies its composition. When music is truly apprehended, virtue and music flourish together. When the gentleman approaches ritual, he approaches it through his heart. In all ritual that has form, that which is formless brings its essence together. When ritual is truly apprehended, virtue and ritual prosper together. This is what is meant by attaining both ritual and music; this is what is meant by possessing virtue. Here one sees the profundity of the gentleman’s subtle understanding of music.

Moreover, the gentleman’s attainment of ritual and music is not confined to his own person and heart. He extends and fully develops it: through consummate ritual, without yielding precedence, all under Heaven is ordered; through consummate music, without sound, all under Heaven is harmonious. The myriad things each find their proper place, and Heaven and Earth are thereby made manifest. When virtue reaches this point, nothing can surpass its fullness. Such is the achievement of equilibrium and harmony in establishing proper positions and nurturing all things, and the Way of embodying trustworthiness and bringing accord to full realization.

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
事君先資其言拜自獻其身以成其信
陳雲鶚
同考試官教諭成批此作詞意剴切若自陳心事
者乎他日殆能成信者耶
考試官教授韓批明晰莊重
考試官教授劉批雅鬯可式
君子之事上也務實其言而已夫言從而行之
則所言爲不虛矣其斯以爲純臣矣乎聖人言
此以立爲臣之準也意以人臣之事君也有自
===
許之訏謨所以虔其始有自靖之大節所以厚
其終故當其筮仕也致君之策已備於素養矣
於是形之論列以爲委質之資澤民之具已脩
於前定矣於是見之敷言以爲效用之本幸際
時之不偶而輸誠於立朝之初今日有稽之言
皆他時可底之績也感明主之見知而矢志於
策名之始一時已試之略皆終身可行之規也
自許如此而自效容可苟哉于焉稽首以受其
命自獻以致其身上弼之君則苟利社稷遑恤
punctuated:
事君，先資其言，拜自獻其身，以成其信。
陳雲鶚
同考試官教諭成批：此作詞意剴切，若自陳心事者乎？他日殆能成信者耶？
考試官教授韓批：明晰莊重。
考試官教授劉批：雅鬯可式。
君子之事上也，務實其言而已。夫言從而行之，則所言爲不虛矣，其斯以爲純臣矣乎？聖人言此，以立爲臣之準也。意以人臣之事君也，有自許之訏謨，所以虔其始；有自靖之大節，所以厚其終。故當其筮仕也，致君之策已備於素養矣，於是形之論列，以爲委質之資；澤民之具已脩於前定矣，於是見之敷言，以爲效用之本。幸際時之不偶，而輸誠於立朝之初，今日有稽之言，皆他時可底之績也；感明主之見知，而矢志於策名之始，一時已試之略，皆終身可行之規也。自許如此，而自效容可苟哉？于焉稽首以受其命，自獻以致其身。上弼之君，則苟利社稷，遑恤
translation_en:
“In serving a ruler, one first presents one’s words, then bows and offers oneself in service, thereby fulfilling one’s pledge.”
Chen Yun’e
Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor, comments: “The language and meaning of this composition are earnest and pointed. Might he be declaring what is in his own heart? Perhaps in days to come he will indeed fulfill his pledge?”
Examiner Han, Professor, comments: “Clear, lucid, dignified, and weighty.”
Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “Elegant and fluent; worthy to serve as a model.”
In serving his superior, the gentleman strives only to give substance to his words. If he follows his words with action, what he has said will not prove empty. Is this not what makes a wholly devoted minister? The Sage said this to establish a standard for those who serve as ministers. His meaning is that, in serving a ruler, a minister has grand plans to which he commits himself, thereby making his beginning reverent; he also has great principles by which he fulfills his own duty, thereby giving substance to his final achievement. Thus, when he first enters office, his plans for bringing his ruler to exemplary government are already complete through his accustomed cultivation. He then sets them forth in reasoned statements as the basis for pledging his service. His means of benefiting the people have already been prepared through prior deliberation. He then expresses them in extended statements as the foundation for rendering effective service. Fortunately encountering an inopportune time [?], he offers his sincerity at the outset of his service at court: everything he says today on a sound basis can become an accomplishment realized in the future. Grateful for an enlightened ruler’s recognition, he pledges his resolve when his name is first entered on the rolls of office: the strategies already tested at that moment are all principles he can follow throughout his life. Having committed himself in this way, how could he be careless in fulfilling that commitment? Thereupon he bows his head to the ground to receive his appointment and offers himself, devoting his person to service. Above, in assisting his ruler, if only it benefits the altars of soil and grain, what leisure has he to concern himself with …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其他也精白承休必此心之無愧而所言之不
虛斯已矣下推之民則有益生民不知有已也
夙夜匪懈必尔位之靖共而所言之克踐斯已
矣官守獻其職焉言責獻其忠焉先資之時此
身已非已有矣則夫不有其身者正所以行如
其言而無負於立朝之初心也內而獻其猷焉
外而獻其力焉拜命之日此身已屬之君矣則
夫能致其身者正所以終如其始而無負於策
名之初志也非所以成其信耶使先言矣而不
===
知所以自獻則無以成其信矣如事君何在昔
古人起莘數語竟著阿衡離巖三篇卒成良弼
言之於先而信之於後遂為天下萬世之純臣
何者其所養者豫也故隱居無求志之實斯行
義無達道之功
第貳場
論
聖神繼天立極
鄧全策
punctuated:
其他也。精白承休，必此心之無愧，而所言之不虛，斯已矣。下推之民，則有益生民，不知有已也。夙夜匪懈，必尔位之靖共，而所言之克踐，斯已矣。官守獻其職焉，言責獻其忠焉。先資之時，此身已非已有矣，則夫不有其身者，正所以行如其言，而無負於立朝之初心也。內而獻其猷焉，外而獻其力焉。拜命之日，此身已屬之君矣，則夫能致其身者，正所以終如其始，而無負於策名之初志也。非所以成其信耶？使先言矣，而不知所以自獻，則無以成其信矣，如事君何？在昔古人，起莘數語，竟著阿衡；離巖三篇，卒成良弼。言之於先，而信之於後，遂為天下萬世之純臣。何者？其所養者豫也。故隱居無求志之實，斯行義無達道之功。

第貳場
論
聖神繼天立極
鄧全策
translation_en:
…anything else. With a pure heart he receives imperial favor, seeking only that his conscience be clear and that his words prove true. Extending his efforts downward to the people, he benefits their lives without a thought for himself. Tireless morning and night, he seeks only to discharge his office reverently and to put his words into practice. Those entrusted with official duties offer their service; those charged with remonstrance offer their loyalty. At the time of his initial appointment [?], his person already ceases to belong to himself. Thus, no longer treating his person as his own is precisely how he acts in accordance with his words and remains true to his original resolve upon entering court service. Serving within the court, he offers his counsel; serving outside it, he offers his strength. From the day he receives his appointment, his person already belongs to his ruler. Thus, being able to devote himself wholly is precisely how he ends as he began and remains true to his original aspiration when his name was entered on the rolls of office. Is this not how he makes good his word? If he first speaks but does not know how to offer himself in service, he has no means of making good his word. How, then, can he serve his ruler?

In antiquity, one man rose from Shen and, with a few words, ultimately distinguished himself as Aheng; another left the cliffs and, through three chapters, ultimately became a worthy counselor. They spoke first and afterward proved true to their words, thereby becoming wholly devoted ministers for all the world and all generations. Why was this? Because they had cultivated themselves beforehand. Thus, if living in seclusion lacks the substance of pursuing one’s aspiration, acting righteously will lack the achievement of bringing the Way into effect.

Second Session
Discourse
The Sagely and Divine Ruler Succeeds Heaven and Establishes the Supreme Standard
Deng Quance

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭陳批聖神繼天承統傳心之要道未
易形容士子類掇浮言莫得肯綮此作獨能闡發其精
蘊且精湛典麗雄渾古健不類時作可爲多士式矣錄之
考試官教授韓批圓活若隋珠溫潤若楚玉蓋佳作也
考試官教授劉批聖神精蘊士子能發之殆於心有得者
道其原于天而具于心乎聖人所以得統于天
而爲萬世法者亦惟其心之純乎理而已是理
也本於天散於物統會於人心心有萬變而理
則至一無二者也理一也而天下之動常病於
===
===
不一者太極之理本無不一而夫人自二之也
聖人亦人也得統于天而人極立焉是聖人功
用之大非夫人所得而及也人見聖人功用之
大也以爲聖人有大異於人者而不知亦惟以
其理之一者純之於心耳然則聖人固不能異
天下而立之極亦不能外一理以達乎天固自
有心極存焉而萬世之極在是矣夫所謂理之
一者何也曰中也中也者太極之本然天下之
正理也聖人以是中而會之於心故曰聖人之
punctuated:
同考試官教諭陳批：聖神繼天，承統傳心之要道，未易形容。士子類掇浮言，莫得肯綮。此作獨能闡發其精蘊，且精湛典麗，雄渾古健，不類時作，可爲多士式矣。錄之。
考試官教授韓批：圓活若隋珠，溫潤若楚玉，蓋佳作也。
考試官教授劉批：聖神精蘊，士子能發之，殆於心有得者。
道其原于天而具于心乎？聖人所以得統于天而爲萬世法者，亦惟其心之純乎理而已。是理也，本於天，散於物，統會於人心。心有萬變，而理則至一無二者也。理一也，而天下之動常病於不一者，太極之理本無不一，而夫人自二之也。聖人亦人也，得統于天而人極立焉，是聖人功用之大，非夫人所得而及也。人見聖人功用之大也，以爲聖人有大異於人者，而不知亦惟以其理之一者純之於心耳。然則聖人固不能異天下而立之極，亦不能外一理以達乎天。固自有心，極存焉，而萬世之極在是矣。夫所謂理之一者何也？曰：中也。中也者，太極之本然，天下之正理也。聖人以是中而會之於心，故曰：聖人之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: The essential Way by which the sages and divine worthies succeeded Heaven, inherited the succession, and transmitted the mind is not easy to describe. Candidates generally piece together empty words without reaching the heart of the matter. This composition alone elucidates its profound essentials. Moreover, it is penetrating and refined, classically elegant, majestic and full-bodied, with an antique vigor. Unlike contemporary compositions, it can serve as a model for the candidates. Record it.

Examiner Han, Professor, comments: Rounded and lively as the pearl of Sui, warm and lustrous as the jade of Chu: this is indeed an excellent composition.

Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: This candidate can elucidate the profound essentials of the sages and divine worthies; he must have attained an understanding of them in his own mind.

Does not the Way originate in Heaven and reside fully in the mind? That by which the sage receives the succession from Heaven and becomes a model for all ages is simply the mind’s complete conformity to principle. This principle has its root in Heaven, is dispersed among things, and is gathered into unity in the human mind. The mind undergoes myriad changes, but principle is utterly one, without duality. Principle is one; yet the activities of the world are constantly afflicted by disunity. This is because the principle of the Supreme Ultimate is fundamentally never other than one, but people themselves divide it.

The sage too is human. He receives the succession from Heaven, and the ultimate standard for humanity is established. Such is the greatness of the sage’s efficacy, which ordinary people cannot attain. Seeing this great efficacy, people suppose that the sage possesses something vastly different from other human beings. They do not understand that he merely brings the unity of principle to purity within his mind. Thus the sage certainly cannot establish an ultimate standard apart from the world, nor can he reach Heaven outside the one principle. Wherever there is a mind, the ultimate standard is inherently present; herein lies the ultimate standard for all ages.

What, then, is meant by the unity of principle? The answer is centrality. Centrality is the original condition of the Supreme Ultimate and the correct principle of all under Heaven. The sage gathers this centrality into unity within his mind. Hence it is said: “The sage’s …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
心純乎理也朱子序中庸而曰上古聖神繼天
立極所以見道統之傳其所由來者遠也且夫
道統之傳曷昉乎生人之初道在天地渾渾焉
噩噩焉不可得而名之孰可得而傳之也迨夫
風氣日開聖人始生聖人者稟二氣之精含五
行之秀備聰明睿智之質夫固天所獨厚而非
天私於聖人也蓋將作之君師以為斯道計耳
聖人之生也有所自故其出也有所為而繼天
立極之功於是乎獨歸於聖人矣夫天之道至
===
神也而聖人何以繼乎天天下至大而千萬世
至遠也而聖人何以立其極噫聖人之所以為
聖人蓋必有所以為之者矣而非人力私智之
所及也易曰先天而天弗違後天而奉天時言
聖人之所以合天也又曰聖人以神道設教而
天下服言聖人之所以感人心也至於言天則
曰一陰一陽之謂道言人則曰繼之者善成之
者性是可見天之所以為道即人之所以為性
而聖人之所以繼天立極者必不能有加于性
punctuated: 心純乎理也。朱子序中庸而曰：「上古聖神，繼天立極。」所以見道統之傳，其所由來者遠也。且夫道統之傳曷昉乎？生人之初，道在天地，渾渾焉，噩噩焉，不可得而名之，孰可得而傳之也？迨夫風氣日開，聖人始生。聖人者，稟二氣之精，含五行之秀，備聰明睿智之質。夫固天所獨厚，而非天私於聖人也，蓋將作之君師，以為斯道計耳。聖人之生也有所自，故其出也有所為，而繼天立極之功於是乎獨歸於聖人矣。夫天之道至神也，而聖人何以繼乎天？天下至大，而千萬世至遠也，而聖人何以立其極？噫！聖人之所以為聖人，蓋必有所以為之者矣，而非人力私智之所及也。《易》曰：「先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時。」言聖人之所以合天也。又曰：「聖人以神道設教，而天下服。」言聖人之所以感人心也。至於言天，則曰：「一陰一陽之謂道。」言人，則曰：「繼之者善，成之者性。」是可見天之所以為道，即人之所以為性，而聖人之所以繼天立極者，必不能有加于性
translation_en:
…the mind is wholly in accord with principle. In his preface to the Doctrine of the Mean, Master Zhu wrote: “The sages and divine men of high antiquity carried on Heaven’s work and established the ultimate standard.” This shows how far back the transmission of the succession of the Way extends. When, then, did this transmission begin? At the beginning of human life, the Way existed within Heaven and Earth, undifferentiated and unformed. It could not be named; who could have transmitted it? Only as the prevailing influences gradually unfolded did sages first arise. Sages receive the pure essence of the two vital forces, embody the finest qualities of the Five Phases, and possess intelligence, discernment, and wisdom. Heaven indeed endows them with exceptional generosity, yet this is no favoritism toward sages. Rather, Heaven intends to make them rulers and teachers, providing thereby for this Way. The birth of sages has its source, and so their emergence has its purpose. Thus the achievement of carrying on Heaven’s work and establishing the ultimate standard belongs uniquely to sages.

Heaven’s Way is supremely wondrous: how, then, can sages carry on Heaven’s work? All under Heaven is vast, and thousands upon thousands of generations stretch far into the future: how can sages establish their ultimate standard? Ah! There must be something by which sages become sages, something beyond the reach of human effort and private cleverness. The Book of Changes says: “When he acts before Heaven, Heaven does not go against him; when he acts after Heaven, he follows Heaven’s seasons.” This speaks of how the sage accords with Heaven. It also says: “The sage establishes instruction through the numinous Way, and all under Heaven submit.” This speaks of how the sage moves human hearts. When speaking of Heaven, it says: “One yin and one yang are called the Way.” When speaking of human beings, it says: “What continues it is goodness; what brings it to completion is human nature.” From this we can see that what constitutes the Way in Heaven constitutes nature in human beings, and that the means by which sages carry on Heaven’s work and establish the ultimate standard necessarily cannot add anything to their nature…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
分之外也上古之世聖神迭興曰庖犧氏曰神
農氏曰黃帝曰堯曰舜是數聖人者皆天命爲
億兆之君師而繼天立極者也此道統所自來
也人見數聖人之治天下也變而通神而化禮
不相襲而樂不相沿也則曰聖人有異道而不
知此可以語其迹耳而非所以語其心也自今
觀之八卦以畫蓋天以象甲歷以推中星以考
璣衡以在何莫而非聖神理天之法也而其以
心相授受者不在是也州野以分步畝以制水
===
土以平山川以奠土壤以則何莫而非聖神理
地之法也而其以心相授受者不在是也書契
以治棟宇以居衣裳以垂弧矢以威耒耜以利
鍾律以和何莫而非聖神理人之法也而其以
心相授受者不在是也聖人之以心相授受者
何哉亦曰理而已矣盍觀之堯舜乎曰允執厥
中云者堯之所以命舜也曰惟精惟一允執厥
中云者舜之所以命禹也夫堯舜所與相告戒
者一中之外無聞焉是豈有所秘而不傳者哉
punctuated:
分之外也。上古之世，聖神迭興，曰庖犧氏，曰神農氏，曰黃帝，曰堯，曰舜。是數聖人者，皆天命爲億兆之君師，而繼天立極者也。此道統所自來也。人見數聖人之治天下也，變而通，神而化，禮不相襲，而樂不相沿也，則曰聖人有異道，而不知此可以語其迹耳，而非所以語其心也。
自今觀之，八卦以畫，蓋天以象，甲歷以推，中星以考，璣衡以在，何莫而非聖神理天之法也？而其以心相授受者不在是也。州野以分，步畝以制，水土以平，山川以奠，土壤以則，何莫而非聖神理地之法也？而其以心相授受者不在是也。書契以治，棟宇以居，衣裳以垂，弧矢以威，耒耜以利，鍾律以和，何莫而非聖神理人之法也？而其以心相授受者不在是也。
聖人之以心相授受者何哉？亦曰理而已矣。盍觀之堯舜乎？曰「允執厥中」云者，堯之所以命舜也；曰「惟精惟一，允執厥中」云者，舜之所以命禹也。夫堯舜所與相告戒者，一中之外無聞焉。是豈有所秘而不傳者哉？
translation_en:
…beyond the bounds of their innate nature. In high antiquity, sages of spiritual insight arose in succession: Paoxi, Shennong, the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun. These sages were all appointed by Heaven as rulers and teachers of the myriad people, carrying on Heaven’s work and establishing the supreme standard. This is the origin of the succession of the Way. People see how these sages governed the world—adapting through change and transforming through spiritual efficacy, neither inheriting one another’s rites nor continuing one another’s music—and conclude that the sages followed different Ways. They do not understand that these things allow us to speak only of their outward deeds, not of their minds.
Viewed from the present, the drawing of the Eight Trigrams, the representation of heaven as a canopy, calculations using the cyclical calendar, observations of stars crossing the meridian, and examinations using the celestial sphere and sighting tube: which of these was not a method by which the sages of spiritual insight ordered celestial affairs? Yet what they transmitted and received from mind to mind did not lie in these things. The division of regions and countryside, the establishment of measures of land in paces and mu, the regulation of waters and lands, the settling of mountains and rivers, and the classification of soils: which of these was not a method by which the sages of spiritual insight ordered the earth? Yet what they transmitted and received from mind to mind did not lie in these things. Written records for government, buildings for habitation, robes and skirts hanging from the body, bows and arrows to inspire awe, plows to benefit the people, and bells and pitch standards to produce harmony: which of these was not a method by which the sages of spiritual insight ordered human affairs? Yet what they transmitted and received from mind to mind did not lie in these things.
What, then, did the sages transmit and receive from mind to mind? It was simply principle. Why not consider Yao and Shun? The words “Sincerely hold fast to the Mean” were Yao’s charge to Shun. The words “Be discerning, be single-minded; sincerely hold fast to the Mean” were Shun’s charge to Yu. In the admonitions that Yao and Shun passed on, we hear of nothing beyond this one Mean. Could it be that they kept something secret and did not transmit it?

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
夫亦以天下之理莫大於中耳蓋是中也天之
命也人之心也三極之矩也羲農以來相傳之
心法也堯以其得於天者而傳之舜舜以其得
於堯者而傳之禹聖聖相承守而不失會於心
達於政光被於四表風動於四方莫非道也而
亦莫非中也是故天敘有典聖人有以惇之而
天下後世五典之極立矣天秩有禮聖人有以
庸之而天下後世五禮之極立矣天命有德討
有罪聖人有以章之用之而天下後世五服五
===
刑之極立矣推而至於人時之授律度之同四
岳之咨九功之敘大章大韶之作孰非天之道
也孰非天下後世之極也指斯道之的開聖學
之源立生民之命垂萬世斯文之統繼天立極
之功孰有大於堯舜而亦何者而非一理之所
爲哉向使洪荒之世堯舜不作則執中之旨孰
濬其源精一之訓孰昭其軌後世將紛拏諆厖
貿貿焉莫知所取衷矣惟夫有堯舜焉以立極
于其上也是以禹湯文武之爲君臯陶伊傅周
punctuated: 夫亦以天下之理莫大於中耳。蓋是中也，天之命也，人之心也，三極之矩也，羲農以來相傳之心法也。堯以其得於天者而傳之舜，舜以其得於堯者而傳之禹，聖聖相承，守而不失，會於心，達於政，光被於四表，風動於四方，莫非道也，而亦莫非中也。是故天敘有典，聖人有以惇之，而天下後世五典之極立矣；天秩有禮，聖人有以庸之，而天下後世五禮之極立矣；天命有德，討有罪，聖人有以章之、用之，而天下後世五服五刑之極立矣。推而至於人時之授、律度之同、四岳之咨、九功之敘、大章大韶之作，孰非天之道也？孰非天下後世之極也？指斯道之的，開聖學之源，立生民之命，垂萬世斯文之統，繼天立極之功，孰有大於堯舜？而亦何者而非一理之所爲哉？向使洪荒之世，堯舜不作，則執中之旨孰濬其源？精一之訓孰昭其軌？後世將紛拏諆厖，貿貿焉莫知所取衷矣。惟夫有堯舜焉，以立極于其上也，是以禹湯文武之爲君，臯陶伊傅周
translation_en:
…It is simply because no principle under Heaven is greater than the Mean. This Mean is Heaven’s mandate, the human heart, the rule governing the three ultimate powers—Heaven, Earth, and humankind—and the teaching of the heart transmitted since Fuxi and Shennong. Yao transmitted to Shun what he had received from Heaven; Shun transmitted to Yu what he had received from Yao. Sage succeeded sage, preserving it without loss, comprehending it in the heart and realizing it in government. Its radiance reached the outermost bounds, and its influence stirred the four quarters like the wind. All of this was the Way, and all of it was the Mean.

Thus, Heaven established the order of human relationships, and the sages strengthened it, establishing the supreme standard for the five relationships throughout the world and for later generations. Heaven established the hierarchy of rites, and the sages put it into practice, establishing the supreme standard for the five rites throughout the world and for later generations. Heaven charged the virtuous with office and punished the guilty; the sages distinguished the former with insignia and applied punishments to the latter, establishing the supreme standard for the five grades of ceremonial robes and the five punishments throughout the world and for later generations. Extending this to announcing the seasons for human labors, standardizing pitch pipes and measures, consulting the Four Mountain Chiefs, ordering the nine achievements, and composing the music of the Great Zhang and the Great Shao—which of these was not Heaven’s Way? Which was not a supreme standard for the world and later generations?

They identified the goal of this Way, opened the source of sagely learning, secured the life and destiny of the people, and transmitted the succession of this cultural tradition for ten thousand generations. Whose achievement in carrying on Heaven’s work and establishing the supreme standard exceeded that of Yao and Shun? And which part of it was not the working of the single principle? Had Yao and Shun not arisen in the primeval age, who would have plumbed the source of the purport of holding fast to the Mean? Who would have illuminated the course prescribed by the injunction to be discerning and single-minded? Later generations would have been entangled in disorder and confusion [?], bewildered and unable to know where to find a sound standard. It was precisely because Yao and Shun established the supreme standard above them that Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu served as rulers, and Gao Yao, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, and the Duke of Zhou …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
召之爲臣相繼代作或得之而爲祗台爲建中
爲敬止爲建極而主治于上焉或得之而爲邁
種爲一德爲主善爲碩膚爲篤棐而輔治于下
焉皆所謂繼志述事濟美乎堯舜者也蓋理至
於中則千聖一心道至於堯舜則千古一極道
之所以昭於日星流於江河而不至於晦且絕
者何者而非堯舜之遺也及周之叔季而有仲
尼者出祖述憲章垂世立敎雖不得君師之位
而繼往開來之功有賢於堯舜者子思子憂道
===
學之失其傳也於是取仲尼之遺訓而中庸作
焉曰擇善曰固執曰時中曰致中曰用中無非
所以推明堯舜以來相傳之意蓋精一執中之
旨至堯舜而始發率性脩道之論至子思而益
明此子思所以有功於堯舜也朱子推原道統
之傳始于聖神繼天立極而要歸於堯舜之執
中朱子之心其亦子思之心乎雖然此聖人事
也學者由擇善以致其精由固執以守其一二
者交致其功而無間焉則中道可以馴致而堯
punctuated: 召之爲臣，相繼代作，或得之而爲祗台，爲建中，爲敬止，爲建極，而主治于上焉；或得之而爲邁種，爲一德，爲主善，爲碩膚，爲篤棐，而輔治于下焉。皆所謂繼志述事，濟美乎堯舜者也。蓋理至於中，則千聖一心；道至於堯舜，則千古一極。道之所以昭於日星，流於江河，而不至於晦且絕者，何者而非堯舜之遺也？及周之叔季，而有仲尼者出，祖述憲章，垂世立敎。雖不得君師之位，而繼往開來之功，有賢於堯舜者。子思子憂道學之失其傳也，於是取仲尼之遺訓，而《中庸》作焉。曰擇善，曰固執，曰時中，曰致中，曰用中，無非所以推明堯舜以來相傳之意。蓋精一執中之旨，至堯舜而始發；率性脩道之論，至子思而益明。此子思所以有功於堯舜也。朱子推原道統之傳，始于聖神繼天立極，而要歸於堯舜之執中。朱子之心，其亦子思之心乎？雖然，此聖人事也。學者由擇善以致其精，由固執以守其一，二者交致其功而無間焉，則中道可以馴致，而堯
translation_en:
…and Shao serving as ministers arose in succession through the ages. Some grasped it and put it into practice by “reverently attending to me,” “establishing the mean,” “resting in reverence,” and “establishing the supreme standard,” thus presiding over government from above. Others grasped it and put it into practice by “vigorously sowing virtue,” “making virtue one,” “taking goodness as their guide,” “achieving great merit,” and “giving devoted assistance,” thus assisting government from below. These were all what is meant by carrying on the intentions and completing the undertakings of Yao and Shun, continuing their excellence. For when principle attains the mean, the thousand sages share one mind; when the Way reaches Yao and Shun, all ages possess a single supreme standard. That the Way shines like the sun and stars and flows like the rivers, without becoming obscured or cut off—what part of this is not the legacy of Yao and Shun?

In the declining age of the Zhou, Zhongni arose. He transmitted the teachings of his predecessors and took their institutions as his model, establishing teachings to be handed down through the ages. Although he did not attain the position of ruler and teacher, his achievement in carrying forward the past and opening the way for the future in some respects surpassed that of Yao and Shun. Master Zisi feared that the transmission of the learning of the Way would be lost. He therefore gathered Zhongni’s surviving teachings and composed the Doctrine of the Mean. Its teachings on choosing the good, holding fast to it, being timely in attaining the mean, bringing the mean to fulfillment, and applying the mean all elucidate the intent transmitted since Yao and Shun. The purport of being discerning and single-minded and holding fast to the mean first emerged with Yao and Shun; the account of following one’s nature and cultivating the Way became clearer still with Zisi. This is how Zisi rendered service to Yao and Shun.

Master Zhu traced the transmission of the succession of the Way to its source, beginning with the sage and divine rulers who succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard, and taking Yao and Shun’s holding fast to the mean as its essential conclusion. Was not Master Zhu’s mind also the mind of Zisi? Yet these are the undertakings of sages. Learners attain discernment by choosing the good and preserve their single-mindedness by holding fast to it. If these two practices work together without interruption, the Way of the mean can gradually be attained, and Yao…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
舜其在我矣乃若博物洽聞以爲精離形去智
以爲一是自陷於支離虚妄而不可與入堯舜
之道非所以道中庸也
表
擬宋以文彦博富弼平章事翰林學士歐
陽脩賀表至和二年
陳文彬
同考試官教諭陳批發揮有宋君臣情誼真篤
考試官教授韓批鏗鏘有金石聲是衆中之純佳者
===
考試官教授劉批駢麗精切渾厚典雅
至和二年某月日翰林學士臣歐陽脩恭
遇
聖明以文彦博富弼同中書門下平章事謹上
言稱
賀者伏以
黄扉宅俊經綸闡
黼黻之猷
絳闕宣麻弼亮集珪璋之彦耆舊同登于一
punctuated:
舜其在我矣。乃若博物洽聞以爲精，離形去智以爲一，是自陷於支離虚妄，而不可與入堯舜之道，非所以道中庸也。

表
擬宋以文彦博富弼平章事翰林學士歐陽脩賀表，至和二年。
陳文彬

同考試官教諭陳批：發揮有宋君臣情誼真篤。
考試官教授韓批：鏗鏘有金石聲，是衆中之純佳者。
考試官教授劉批：駢麗精切，渾厚典雅。

至和二年某月日，翰林學士臣歐陽脩恭遇聖明以文彦博富弼同中書門下平章事，謹上言稱賀者。伏以：黄扉宅俊，經綸闡黼黻之猷；絳闕宣麻，弼亮集珪璋之彦。耆舊同登于一
translation_en:
…Shun would then be within me. But to regard extensive knowledge and wide learning as refinement, and abandonment of bodily form and intellect as unity, is to entrap oneself in fragmentation and empty delusion. Such people cannot enter the Way of Yao and Shun; this is no means of practicing the Mean.

Memorial
A congratulatory memorial composed in the persona of the Song Hanlin Academician Ouyang Xiu, on the appointment of Wen Yanbo and Fu Bi as Managers of Affairs, in the second year of Zhihe [1055].
By Chen Wenbin.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “It brings out the truly profound affection between the Song ruler and his ministers.”
Comment by Examiner Han, Professor: “It rings with the resonance of bronze and stone chimes; among the submissions, this is an unalloyed example of excellence.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “Elegant in its parallel phrasing, precise and apt; rich, substantial, stately, and refined.”

On a certain day and month in the second year of Zhihe, your servant Ouyang Xiu, Hanlin Academician, respectfully submits this memorial of congratulation on the occasion of Your Sagacious Majesty’s appointment of Wen Yanbo and Fu Bi as Managers of Affairs of the Secretariat–Chancellery.

I humbly consider: Worthy men take their places behind the yellow doors of the chief ministers’ offices; their ordering of affairs unfolds plans that lend embroidered splendor to imperial rule. At the crimson palace gates, appointment edicts are proclaimed; men as excellent as jade tablets assemble to assist and enlighten the sovereign. The venerable veterans rise together on a single…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
日
明良遘會乎千年鼎鉉光流章縫喜溢臣脩誠
懽誠忭稽首頓首竊以設官以爲民極立
政在人疏爵以代天工良臣惟聖矧此中
書政本尤爲下民具瞻紫極躔輝上應三
台之象彤墀簉羽班先八座之尊佐
一人以理萬幾陶融景化正六符而調四序燮
贊陰陽自非柱石之英曷稱樞機之選虞
庭枚卜阿閣呈鳳儀之祥傅野鹽梅彤日
===
消雉雊之沴一德交孚于載亳爲式九圍
二公分治乎成周永清四海蓋人主職先
論相惟王者能自得師末世風微鼎實希
聞良弼
熈朝運啟泰征雅重元僚顧人才未易周知
而來章難於有慶躍龍騄驥自昔徒誇求
馬得麟于今僅見伏念臣彥博臣弼王佐
良才大臣雅量朴忠自許天下皆知可用
之賢仁智不凡丱歲卽動時人之望撫綏
punctuated: 日，明良遘會乎千年。鼎鉉光流，章縫喜溢。臣脩誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首。竊以設官以爲民極，立政在人；疏爵以代天工，良臣惟聖。矧此中書政本，尤爲下民具瞻。紫極躔輝，上應三台之象；彤墀簉羽，班先八座之尊。佐一人以理萬幾，陶融景化；正六符而調四序，燮贊陰陽。自非柱石之英，曷稱樞機之選？虞庭枚卜，阿閣呈鳳儀之祥；傅野鹽梅，彤日消雉雊之沴。一德交孚于載亳，爲式九圍；二公分治乎成周，永清四海。蓋人主職先論相，惟王者能自得師。末世風微，鼎實希聞良弼；熈朝運啟，泰征雅重元僚。顧人才未易周知，而來章難於有慶。躍龍騄驥，自昔徒誇；求馬得麟，于今僅見。伏念臣彥博、臣弼，王佐良才，大臣雅量。朴忠自許，天下皆知可用之賢；仁智不凡，丱歲卽動時人之望。撫綏
translation_en: …day; an enlightened sovereign and worthy ministers meet in an encounter such as comes once in a thousand years. Radiance streams from the cauldron’s handles—the chief ministers—and joy overflows among the scholars in their ceremonial caps. Your servant Xiu, truly delighted and truly rejoicing, bows his head to the ground and prostrates himself. I humbly consider that offices are established to provide a standard for the people: establishing government depends upon finding the right men. Ranks are bestowed so that men may perform Heaven’s work on its behalf: worthy ministers depend upon a sage sovereign. How much more does this apply to the Secretariat, the foundation of government, toward which all the people look! Its brilliance moves about the Purple Pole, corresponding above to the Three Terraces constellation; its ranks assemble like ordered wings upon the vermilion steps, taking precedence over the exalted Eight Seats. Assisting the One Man in managing the myriad affairs, its ministers nurture glorious transformation; setting right the Six Signs and harmonizing the four seasons, they help bring yin and yang into accord. Unless they are outstanding men who can serve as pillars of the state, how could they merit selection for its central offices? When candidates were divined individually at Shun’s court, the lofty pavilion displayed the auspicious appearance of a phoenix; when the man from Fuye served as salt and plums to season government, the ‘vermilion sun’ [?] dispelled the baleful portent of the crowing pheasant. Sovereign and minister trusted one another through their single virtue at ‘Zai Bo’ [?], providing a model for the nine regions; the two dukes divided the governance of Chengzhou, bringing lasting peace within the four seas. For a ruler’s foremost duty is to assess his chief ministers, and only a true king can find a teacher for himself. In declining ages, this tradition weakened, and worthy assistants were seldom heard of among those who filled the ministerial cauldron. With the opening of our flourishing dynasty’s fortune, auspicious signs of concord have placed particular weight upon its foremost ministers. Yet men’s talents are not easily known in full, and incoming commendations [?] can rarely furnish grounds for congratulation. Leaping dragon-steeds and fleet coursers have, since antiquity, too often been empty boasts; to seek a horse and obtain a qilin is something scarcely witnessed until today. I humbly reflect that your servants Wen Yanbo and Fu Bi possess the fine talents needed to assist a king and the noble magnanimity of great ministers. Committed to plain sincerity and loyalty, they are known throughout the realm as worthy men fit for service; extraordinary in benevolence and wisdom, they already inspired their contemporaries’ hopes when their hair was still bound in childhood tufts. Bringing comfort and peace to…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
河北壯猷淨掃潢池奉使虜廷直節驚傳
朔漠綰銅符于秦益政洽參宣迓竹馬于
青齊功多救濟幸
聖人明見萬里肝膽相加謂宰司位冠羣僚耆
耇是用天開
泰運道合
明時玆蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
膺命冊玄
===
應期握紀紹
列聖重熈之緒
御極餘三十年接千古道統之傳
挺生當五百嵗
乃文乃武欽明上契于神堯
克儉克勤祗德同符乎大禹
御經筵以進講納誨如流
開章閣以延儒求賢若渴富藏四海孝洽
三宮兩儀奠而七曜明太平有象百姓和而萬
punctuated:
河北，壯猷淨掃潢池；奉使虜廷，直節驚傳朔漠。綰銅符于秦益，政洽參宣；迓竹馬于青齊，功多救濟。幸聖人明見萬里，肝膽相加，謂宰司位冠羣僚，耆耇是用。天開泰運，道合明時。
玆蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，膺命冊玄，應期握紀，紹列聖重熈之緒，御極餘三十年；接千古道統之傳，挺生當五百嵗。乃文乃武，欽明上契于神堯；克儉克勤，祗德同符乎大禹。御經筵以進講，納誨如流；開章閣以延儒，求賢若渴。富藏四海，孝洽三宮。兩儀奠而七曜明，太平有象；百姓和而萬
translation_en:
…in Hebei, sweeping away rebellion through mighty strategy; sent as an envoy to the foreign court, he won astonished acclaim throughout the northern desert for his unbending integrity. Holding the bronze tallies of office in Qin and Yi, they spread beneficent government through their provincial service [?]; welcomed by children riding bamboo hobbyhorses in Qing and Qi, they accomplished much in relief and succor. Fortunately, the sage sovereign sees clearly over ten thousand li and treats them with heartfelt trust. Holding that the chief ministers rank above all other officials, he employs these venerable elders. Heaven has opened an era of flourishing fortune; the Way accords with this enlightened age.
This is because we have humbly encountered 〇〇〇〇, who has received the mandate and been invested by Heaven [?], and who, responding to the appointed time, holds the guiding threads of rule. Continuing the accumulated splendor of successive sage sovereigns, you have occupied the throne for more than thirty years; receiving the transmission of the Way handed down through the ages, you have arisen as the outstanding sage who appears once in five hundred years. Accomplished in both civil and military affairs, your reverence and discernment accord with those of divine Yao of old; frugal and diligent, your reverent virtue matches that of Yu the Great. You attend the Classics Colloquium for lectures and receive admonition as readily as flowing water; you open the literary pavilion to invite scholars, thirsting for worthy men. Wealth is stored throughout the realm, and filial devotion extends to the Three Palaces. Heaven and earth stand secure, and the seven luminaries shine: the signs of great peace are manifest. The people live in harmony, and the myriad…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
物理至治無疆念惟輔弼之司實為腹心
之寄爰徵舊德竝晉台階拔彥博于永興
望從中外起富弼于鄭蔡言用縉紳位列
南槐謀斷均調玉燭身依
北斗規隨共轉洪鈞材館瑞氣浮春紫陌歡
聲滿路雲從龍風從虎貞元符會合之期
金作礪旱作霖
喜起洽雍熈之運人惟求舊延登何事乎千
旌
===
===
謀出僉同總攬真賢於夢卜臣幸際
休辰躬逢
景會
天顏有喜咫尺忝近臣之知
帝德難名敷奏愧詞垣之寵聽
綸音而雀躍莫罄颺言望
仙仗以鵷隨惟知舞蹈伏願
主善為師
任賢勿貳
punctuated:
物理，至治無疆。念惟輔弼之司，實為腹心之寄。爰徵舊德，竝晉台階。拔彥博于永興，望從中外；起富弼于鄭蔡，言用縉紳。位列南槐，謀斷均調玉燭；身依北斗，規隨共轉洪鈞。材館瑞氣浮春，紫陌歡聲滿路。雲從龍，風從虎，貞元符會合之期；金作礪，旱作霖，喜起洽雍熈之運。人惟求舊，延登何事乎千旌？謀出僉同，總攬真賢於夢卜。
臣幸際休辰，躬逢景會。天顏有喜，咫尺忝近臣之知；帝德難名，敷奏愧詞垣之寵。聽綸音而雀躍，莫罄颺言；望仙仗以鵷隨，惟知舞蹈。伏願主善為師，任賢勿貳。
translation_en:
…all things are duly ordered, and perfect government knows no bounds. Considering that the offices of chief ministers are truly entrusted with the duties of the heart and vitals, Your Majesty has summoned men of long-established virtue and advanced them together to the highest ministerial ranks. You have raised Yanbo from Yongxing, answering the hopes of those within and beyond the court; you have recalled Fu Bi from Zheng and Cai, heeding the words of the officials. Ranked beside the southern sophora trees, through deliberation and decision they jointly bring the seasons into harmonious accord; standing close to the Northern Dipper, through planning and faithful execution they together turn the great potter’s wheel of creation. Auspicious vapors float like spring over the hall of talent [?], and joyous voices fill the roads of the capital. Clouds follow the dragon, and winds follow the tiger: the renewal of the cosmic cycle accords with this moment of meeting between sovereign and ministers. As a whetstone serves metal, and timely rain relieves drought, their joyful mutual encouragement brings harmony to an age of flourishing peace. In choosing men, seek those long known: what need is there for a thousand banners to invite and advance them? Counsel issues from unanimous agreement; through dreams and divination, truly worthy men are gathered into Your Majesty’s service.
Your servant is fortunate to encounter this blessed time and personally witness this splendid occasion. Your heavenly countenance shows joy; so close to Your Majesty, I am unworthily favored with the recognition accorded an intimate minister. Your imperial virtue is beyond naming; presenting my words, I feel unworthy of the favor bestowed upon me in the Hanlin Academy. Hearing Your imperial utterance, I leap with delight like a sparrow, yet cannot exhaust my praises. Gazing toward Your august ceremonial escort, I follow in the ordered ranks of court officials and can only dance for joy. I humbly pray that You take goodness as Your guide and teacher, and employ the worthy without wavering…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
達四聰明四目堯仁廣運于鈞天
協五紀撫五辰箕福斂時于斗極
天與長而地與久彌
聖壽之萬年
日之升而月之恒鞏
皇圖於億載臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹奉
表稱
===
賀以
聞
第參塲
策〔王道〕
第一問
鄧全策
同考試官教授林 批〔我〕
二祖誠一靜虛心源遠契唐堯我
皇上敬一心學近符
punctuated:
達四聰，明四目，堯仁廣運于鈞天；協五紀，撫五辰，箕福斂時于斗極。天與長而地與久，彌聖壽之萬年；日之升而月之恒，鞏皇圖於億載。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屛營之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。
第參塲
策〔王道〕
第一問
鄧全策
同考試官教授林 批〔我〕
二祖誠一靜虛，心源遠契唐堯；我皇上敬一心學，近符
translation_en:
…Open the hearing to all four quarters and illuminate the sight in all four directions: may benevolence like Yao’s extend throughout the highest heavens. Harmonize the five reckonings of time and regulate the five celestial markers: may the blessings taught by Jizi be gathered at the celestial pole. Enduring with Heaven and lasting with Earth, may Your Majesty’s sacred longevity extend for ten thousand years. Like the rising sun and the constant moon, may the imperial dominion be secured for a hundred million years. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your sacred person, cannot contain his utmost fervor and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to convey my congratulations to Your Majesty.
Third Session
Policy Essay〔The Kingly Way〕
First Question
Policy essay by Deng Quan

The two founding emperors were sincere and single-minded, still and free of preconceptions; the wellspring of their minds accorded with that of Tang Yao in distant antiquity. Our emperor’s learning of the mind, founded on reverent single-mindedness, accords with the more recent example of …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
二祖此作發揚殆盡蓋涵濡
聖化而有得者
考試官教授韓批
帝堯與我
聖上曠世而相感者心學也
精一與
敬一異世而同符者道統也求其闡揚
聖化之隆者惟是作得之子豈粤西士乎
考試官教授劉批我
===
二祖暨我
皇上道法之精得統於天傳心於堯子能敷揚而敘述之其有得於
聖化者深矣
開道統之原者其天乎承心學之傳者其
聖乎天何言哉天不言而示人以於穆不
已之精者莫非其道之所在也聖人何爲
哉聖人無爲而承天以純一不二之懿者
莫非其心學之所傳也故帝王之治莫不
以道爲本帝王之道莫不以心爲事得其
punctuated:
二祖，此作發揚殆盡，蓋涵濡聖化而有得者。
考試官教授韓批：「帝堯與我聖上，曠世而相感者，心學也；精一與敬一，異世而同符者，道統也。求其闡揚聖化之隆者，惟是作得之。子豈粤西士乎？」
考試官教授劉批：「我二祖暨我皇上，道法之精，得統於天，傳心於堯。子能敷揚而敘述之，其有得於聖化者深矣。」
開道統之原者，其天乎？承心學之傳者，其聖乎？天何言哉？天不言而示人以於穆不已之精者，莫非其道之所在也。聖人何爲哉？聖人無爲而承天以純一不二之懿者，莫非其心學之所傳也。故帝王之治，莫不以道爲本；帝王之道，莫不以心爲事。得其
translation_en:
…the Two Imperial Ancestors. This composition expounds the matter almost exhaustively; its author must have been steeped in the sage emperor’s transforming influence and gained something from it.
Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: “What enables Emperor Yao and our sage sovereign to respond to one another across distant ages is the learning of the mind. What makes ‘refinement and single-mindedness’ and ‘reverent single-mindedness’ tally across different ages is the succession of the Way. If we seek a work that fully expounds the greatness of the sage emperor’s transforming influence, this composition alone succeeds. Can you really be a scholar of Yuexi?”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Our Two Imperial Ancestors and our present emperor, in the refinement of their Way and methods, received their succession from Heaven and inherited the transmission of the mind from Yao. You have been able to expound and set this forth: what you have gained from the sage emperor’s transforming influence is profound indeed.”
Is it not Heaven that opens the source of the succession of the Way? Is it not the sage who receives the transmission of the learning of the mind? What does Heaven say? Heaven does not speak, yet the profound and unceasing essence it reveals to humanity is in every instance where its Way resides. What does the sage do? The sage acts without contrivance, yet the excellence of pure single-mindedness, without division, through which he accords with Heaven is in every instance what his learning of the mind transmits. Thus the government of emperors and kings invariably takes the Way as its foundation, and the Way of emperors and kings invariably takes the mind as its concern. Attaining their …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
心則道與治固可得而言矣觀乎此則堯
之所以得統於天開萬世心學之古始
聖祖之所以嗣統於堯超歷世諸君於下風而
我
皇上聖學統天同符
二祖欽若祗
玄直遡帝堯久道化成之效至德淵微之應愚
生雖陋有不可以揄揚其萬一乎請敬陳
之夫自孔子討論墳典之書斷自唐虞而
===
下以上古淳朴隨事為治法度未立至堯
而始明治道因事立法其施政制事皆依
循法則著見功迹可以為後世典常故二
帝之書皆謂之典其敘堯之治曰放勳賛
堯之德曰欽明文思安安者言以此四德
行放勳之事故其所為皆得義理之至當
而謂之安安也不曰聰明而曰欽明與序
言異者蓋立事則欽慎為大舉德則聰明
為先程子亦甞有是言矣然其先天以開
punctuated:
心，則道與治固可得而言矣。觀乎此，則堯之所以得統於天，開萬世心學之古始；聖祖之所以嗣統於堯，超歷世諸君於下風；而我皇上聖學統天，同符二祖，欽若祗玄，直遡帝堯，久道化成之效，至德淵微之應，愚生雖陋，有不可以揄揚其萬一乎？請敬陳之。
夫自孔子討論墳典之書，斷自唐虞而下，以上古淳朴，隨事為治，法度未立，至堯而始明治道，因事立法。其施政制事，皆依循法則，著見功迹，可以為後世典常，故二帝之書皆謂之典。其敘堯之治曰「放勳」，賛堯之德曰「欽明文思安安」者，言以此四德行放勳之事，故其所為皆得義理之至當，而謂之「安安」也。不曰「聰明」而曰「欽明」，與序言異者，蓋立事則欽慎為大，舉德則聰明為先，程子亦甞有是言矣。然其先天以開
translation_en:
…the mind, then surely the Way and governance can be understood and discussed. Viewed in this light, Yao received the succession to the Way from Heaven and inaugurated the learning of the mind for all ages; the Sagely Ancestor inherited that succession from Yao and so surpassed the rulers of successive ages that they stood beneath him. And our Emperor, whose sagely learning unites with Heaven and accords with the Two Founding Ancestors, reverently conforms to and venerates the profound [?], tracing his lineage directly back to Emperor Yao. Though I, an unworthy student, am shallow in learning, could I not extol even a ten-thousandth part of the transforming effects of his enduring adherence to the Way and the profound, subtle manifestations of his consummate virtue? Permit me respectfully to set them forth.
When Confucius examined and discussed the ancient writings known as the Mounds and Canons, he chose to begin with Tang and Yu and proceed onward. This was because, in high antiquity, people were simple and unadorned, governance responded to circumstances as they arose, and laws and institutions had not yet been established. Only with Yao was the Way of governance first made clear and laws established to meet particular circumstances. His administration and management of affairs all followed rules and standards, producing manifest achievements that could serve as enduring norms for later ages. Thus the writings concerning the Two Emperors are both called “Canons.” In recounting Yao’s governance, the text says “vast achievement”; in praising his virtue, it says “reverent, discerning, accomplished, and thoughtful, naturally and effortlessly at ease.” This means that he employed these four virtues to accomplish deeds of vast achievement. Everything he did therefore attained perfect accordance with moral principle and rightness, and so he is described as “naturally and effortlessly at ease.” The text says “reverent and discerning,” rather than “perceptive and discerning,” differing from the wording of the Preface. This is because, in undertaking affairs, reverence and caution are paramount, whereas in enumerating virtues, perceptiveness and discernment come first. Master Cheng also once made this point. Yet in his anticipating Heaven so as to enlighten…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
人因時而立政天之所以作民君師而爲
萬世開太平之治立道統之傳者則欽之
一言該括盡矣益之賛曰帝德廣運乃聖
乃神乃武乃文孔子曰大哉堯之爲君巍
巍乎惟天爲大惟堯則之迹其所以爲聖
神文武而與天同其大者豈能有加於欽
之一言哉夫自脩身齊家以至平天下者
治之道也則始於明俊德而後由睦九族
以和萬邦者皆此欽之爲也建立治綱分
===
正百職至於創制立度盡天下之事者治
之法也則自疇咨以下允釐百工之績以
咸熙庶政者一則曰欽哉二則曰欽哉皆
此心之推也若其爲事之大莫過授受之
際豈不能諄於告戒而侈有論說哉迨其
命舜之辭不過曰天之曆數在爾躬允執
厥中而已曰曆數者求端於天而以其道
統之傳望之也曰執中者求端於心而以
其聖學之要語之也噫堯之所以爲大者
punctuated: 人，因時而立政，天之所以作民君師而爲萬世開太平之治、立道統之傳者，則欽之一言該括盡矣。益之賛曰：「帝德廣運，乃聖乃神，乃武乃文。」孔子曰：「大哉，堯之爲君！巍巍乎！惟天爲大，惟堯則之。」迹其所以爲聖神文武而與天同其大者，豈能有加於欽之一言哉？夫自脩身齊家以至平天下者，治之道也。則始於明俊德，而後由睦九族以和萬邦者，皆此欽之爲也。建立治綱，分正百職，至於創制立度，盡天下之事者，治之法也。則自疇咨以下，允釐百工之績，以咸熙庶政者，一則曰「欽哉」，二則曰「欽哉」，皆此心之推也。若其爲事之大，莫過授受之際，豈不能諄於告戒而侈有論說哉？迨其命舜之辭，不過曰：「天之曆數在爾躬，允執厥中。」而已。曰曆數者，求端於天，而以其道統之傳望之也；曰執中者，求端於心，而以其聖學之要語之也。噫！堯之所以爲大者，
translation_en:
…humankind, and establishing government in accordance with the times: Heaven’s purpose in raising up a ruler and teacher for the people, thereby inaugurating an age of Great Peace for all generations and establishing the transmission of the succession of the Way, is fully encompassed in the single word “reverence.” Yi’s praise reads: “The emperor’s virtue is far-reaching in its operation: sagacious and spiritually perceptive, martial and cultured.” Confucius said: “Great indeed was Yao as a ruler! How lofty! Heaven alone is great, and Yao alone took it as his model.” If we trace what made him sagacious, spiritually perceptive, cultured, and martial, sharing Heaven’s greatness, could anything go beyond this single word, “reverence”?

To cultivate oneself and regulate one’s household, and thereby bring peace to all under Heaven, is the Way of government. Beginning with making illustrious one’s eminent virtue, then bringing harmony to the nine degrees of kinship and, through them, concord to the myriad states—all this is the work of reverence. To establish the guiding principles of government, assign and properly order the hundred offices, and proceed to institute regulations and standards, encompassing all the affairs of the realm, constitutes the methods of government. From his inquiries and consultations onward, he duly ordered the work of the hundred officers so that all branches of government flourished. First he said, “Be reverent!” and again he said, “Be reverent!” All this was the extension of this same heart-and-mind.

As for his greatest undertaking, nothing surpassed the moment of handing over and receiving the throne. Could he not have offered earnest admonitions and lengthy explanations? Yet when he addressed Shun, his words were no more than these: “Heaven’s ordained succession now rests upon your person. Sincerely hold fast to the Mean.” In speaking of the ordained succession, he sought its source in Heaven and looked to Shun to carry on the succession of the Way. In speaking of holding fast to the Mean, he sought its source in the heart-and-mind and instructed Shun in the essentials of sagely learning. Ah! What made Yao great…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
可知矣舜亦以命禹而益之以三言者則
所以發明堯之一言必如是而後盡也惟
聖人之德愈高故其所慎於幾微者愈謹
聖人之心益虛故其所見於告戒者益詳
要之中即欽也精一即所以執也欽不外
乎此心之中執必有假於精一之力帝王
之授受可知也自是而後湯有日新之銘
武王有丹書之戒曰祗台德先曰建中建
極莫非其相傳之心法也下至遜志時敏
===
以求建事宥密緝熈以求顯德其學何學
也莫非其所傳之欽與中也嗣是而漢而
唐若宋其間英君誼辟非無有志於道然
或雜焉而未純或多欲而未至是皆於其
人心道心未有以辨其危微之幾故於其
惟精惟一未能以致其允執之學而所謂
欽者失之放逸所謂中者流於偏倚而不
能無過不及之差奚足以續道統之傳哉
洪惟我
punctuated:
可知矣。舜亦以命禹，而益之以三言者，則所以發明堯之一言，必如是而後盡也。惟聖人之德愈高，故其所慎於幾微者愈謹；聖人之心益虛，故其所見於告戒者益詳。要之，中即欽也，精一即所以執也。欽不外乎此心之中，執必有假於精一之力，帝王之授受可知也。自是而後，湯有日新之銘，武王有丹書之戒，曰「祗台德先」，曰「建中建極」，莫非其相傳之心法也。下至遜志時敏以求建事，宥密緝熈以求顯德，其學何學也？莫非其所傳之欽與中也。嗣是而漢而唐若宋，其間英君誼辟非無有志於道，然或雜焉而未純，或多欲而未至，是皆於其人心道心未有以辨其危微之幾，故於其惟精惟一未能以致其允執之學，而所謂欽者失之放逸，所謂中者流於偏倚，而不能無過不及之差，奚足以續道統之傳哉？
洪惟我
translation_en:
…can thus be understood. Shun likewise used these words to charge Yu, adding three statements to them: only in this way could the meaning of Yao’s single statement be fully elucidated. The loftier the sage’s virtue, the more carefully he attends to the subtlest incipient tendencies; the more receptive the sage’s mind, the more detailed the admonitions in which it finds expression. In essence, the mean is reverence, and refinement and single-mindedness are the means of holding fast to it. Reverence does not extend beyond the mean within this mind; holding fast to it necessarily depends upon the power of refinement and single-mindedness. Thus we can understand what the ancient emperors and kings transmitted and received.
Thereafter, Tang had his inscription on daily renewal, and King Wu had the admonitions of the Cinnabar Writ (Danshu). The sayings “Reverently put my virtue first” and “Establish the mean and establish the ultimate standard” all belong to their transmitted method of cultivating the mind. Further instances include humbling one’s aspirations and constantly striving in learning to accomplish affairs, and cultivating profound tranquillity and continuing illumination to manifest virtue. What was the learning they pursued? It was none other than the reverence and the mean that had been transmitted to them.
Subsequently, during the Han, Tang, and Song, there were indeed outstanding rulers and righteous sovereigns who aspired to the Way. Yet some remained mixed rather than pure, while others had too many desires to attain it. All this arose because they had failed to distinguish the subtle beginnings of the precarious human mind and the elusive mind of the Way. Thus, in refinement and single-mindedness, they could not perfect the learning required truly to hold fast to the mean. What was called reverence was lost through laxity and indulgence; what was called the mean drifted into partiality and bias, inevitably producing errors of excess and deficiency. How could they suffice to continue the transmission of the succession of the Way?
We reverently reflect upon our…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝文武聖神度越百王然於兵戈之
餘卽書衍義于
廡壁而謂學士宋濂曰
朕之爲君上畏天地下畏兆民兢兢業業不敢
自逸而又曰體道凝神誠一弗二其見於
觀心亭記者可知也大要不過曰敬而已
成祖文皇帝道兼作述功並創守仍於萬幾之
暇著爲聖學心法一書而親爲之序其得
學士解縉正心講章則曰心能靜虛自然
===
純是天理是心也卽
太祖誠一弗二之心也上接湯武不傳之緒而
遠遡精一執中之旨則我
二祖之聖學傳心其源有自至我
皇上之神明默契能自得師其天縱欽明之德
固無異於放勳而獨得心法之秘殆有光
於
前聖
敬一有箴心箴有註其曰匪敬弗聚則所謂
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝文武聖神，度越百王，然於兵戈之餘，卽書《衍義》于廡壁，而謂學士宋濂曰：「朕之爲君，上畏天地，下畏兆民，兢兢業業，不敢自逸。」而又曰：「體道凝神，誠一弗二。」其見於《觀心亭記》者可知也。大要不過曰敬而已。
成祖文皇帝道兼作述，功並創守，仍於萬幾之暇，著爲《聖學心法》一書，而親爲之序。其得學士解縉《正心講章》，則曰：「心能靜虛，自然純是天理。」是心也，卽太祖誠一弗二之心也。上接湯武不傳之緒，而遠遡精一執中之旨，則我二祖之聖學傳心，其源有自。
至我皇上之神明默契，能自得師，其天縱欽明之德，固無異於放勳，而獨得心法之秘，殆有光於前聖。《敬一》有箴，《心箴》有註。其曰「匪敬弗聚」，則所謂
translation_en:
…Emperor Gao, Taizu, was accomplished in civil and military affairs, sagely and spiritually perceptive, surpassing the hundred kings. Yet amid respite from warfare, he had the Extended Meaning inscribed on the corridor walls and told Academician Song Lian: “As ruler, above I stand in awe of Heaven and Earth, and below I stand in awe of the myriad people. Vigilant and conscientious, I dare not indulge myself in ease.” He also said: “Embody the Way and concentrate the spirit; be sincere and single-minded, without division.” This can be understood from what appears in his Record of the Pavilion for Contemplating the Mind. Its essential purport amounts simply to reverent attentiveness.
Emperor Wen, Chengzu, united in his Way both originating and transmitting, and in his achievements both founding and preserving. Even amid his myriad affairs, he found leisure to compose The Sagely Learning’s Methods of the Mind and personally wrote its preface. Upon receiving Academician Xie Jin’s Lecture on Rectifying the Mind, he said: “If the mind can be still and empty, it will naturally consist purely of heavenly principle.” This mind was precisely Taizu’s mind of sincerity and single-mindedness, without division. Taking up the interrupted thread of transmission from Tang and Wu, and tracing it farther back to the teaching of refinement, single-mindedness, and holding fast to the mean, our two ancestral emperors’ sagely learning and transmission of the mind thus had an authentic source.
As for our present Emperor, his spiritual understanding accords tacitly with the Way, and he can attain it for himself and serve as a teacher. His Heaven-endowed virtue of reverence and illumination is assuredly no different from that of Fangxun [Yao]; his unique attainment of the secrets of the methods of the mind may indeed add lustre to the sages of old. He has composed an Admonition on Reverence and Single-mindedness and supplied annotations to the Admonition on the Mind. When he says, “Without reverence, nothing can be gathered together,” this refers to what is called…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
欽明文思允恭克讓光于四表格于上下
者皆聚於此矣其曰匪一弗純則所謂疇
咨登庸宅揆亮采夙夜惟寅出入惟允者
皆純於此矣曰畏天勤民不遑寧處是卽
時幾時勅之心也曰靜虛無欲日新不已
是卽兢業弗懈之心也外是而豳風有歌
無逸有記而敬形於
殿亭矣欽天有頌
廟祀有詩而敬形於
===
郊廟矣肆今至治馨香昭著乎靈貺
神化融徹協應乎休徵從古所未有也孔子
於堯曰蕩蕩乎民無能名焉囿於天地者
不知天地之爲大冒於日月者不知日月
之爲明
聖德神功之盛非可以言語形容是猶天地日
月之不可以繪畫而稱贊之也涵泳其化
而莫測其自漸濡其德而莫有其功殆猶
康衢之謠曰不識不知順帝之則而已又
punctuated:
欽明文思，允恭克讓，光于四表，格于上下者，皆聚於此矣。其曰「匪一弗純」，則所謂「疇咨登庸，宅揆亮采，夙夜惟寅，出入惟允」者，皆純於此矣。曰「畏天勤民，不遑寧處」，是卽時幾時勅之心也。曰「靜虛無欲，日新不已」，是卽兢業弗懈之心也。外是而《豳風》有歌，《無逸》有記，而敬形於殿亭矣；《欽天》有頌，廟祀有詩，而敬形於郊廟矣。肆今至治馨香，昭著乎靈貺；神化融徹，協應乎休徵，從古所未有也。
孔子於堯曰：「蕩蕩乎！民無能名焉。」囿於天地者，不知天地之爲大；冒於日月者，不知日月之爲明。聖德神功之盛，非可以言語形容，是猶天地日月之不可以繪畫而稱贊之也。涵泳其化，而莫測其自；漸濡其德，而莫有其功。殆猶康衢之謠曰：「不識不知，順帝之則。」而已。又
translation_en:
…those qualities described as “reverent and discerning, accomplished and thoughtful, truly respectful and capable of yielding, with a radiance reaching the four outer bounds and extending above and below” are all gathered here. His statement, “Without unity, there is no purity,” means that the qualities described as “consulting widely and raising the worthy to office, occupying the chief minister’s position and assisting in affairs, remaining reverent morning and night, and trustworthy in going out and coming in” are all made pure here. He says, “Stand in awe of Heaven and labor diligently for the people, with no leisure to rest at ease”: this is precisely the mind attentive to the first stirrings of affairs and ever vigilant. He says, “Be still and empty, without desires, renewing oneself daily without cease”: this is precisely the mind that remains watchful and diligent, never slackening. Beyond these, there are songs on the Airs of Bin and a record on Against Idleness, through which reverence takes visible form in halls and pavilions; there is a eulogy on Revering Heaven and poetry on sacrifices in the ancestral temple, through which reverence takes visible form at the suburban altars and ancestral temples. Thus today the sweet fragrance of perfect government is manifest in divine blessings; his wondrous transforming influence penetrates everywhere, answered harmoniously by auspicious signs. Such things have never existed since antiquity.
Confucius said of Yao: “So vast was he! The people could find no name for him.” Those encompassed by Heaven and Earth do not know the greatness of Heaven and Earth; those beneath the sun and moon do not know the brilliance of the sun and moon. The fullness of His Majesty’s sagely virtue and wondrous achievements cannot be represented in words, just as Heaven and Earth, the sun and moon, cannot be adequately praised through painting. Immersed in his transforming influence, people cannot fathom its source; steeped in his virtue, they have no achievement to call their own. It is much as the Song of the Broad Thoroughfare says: “Without conscious knowledge or understanding, we follow the sovereign’s standards”—and nothing more. And furthermore…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
何敢區區較其欽之與敬執之與一其孰
爲在堯之德而孰爲在我
聖天子之心法也哉先聖後聖其揆一也世不
必同也善繼善述其道一也時不必同也
故謂我
皇上之敬一得統於堯焉同符於
二祖焉可也謂我
皇上之心學獨得於天焉百世以俟焉亦可也
抑宋儒蔡氏有言敬者天之所福百祥之
===
所集也蓋人之一心有所敬畏則精神思
慮日由乎天理之中而躬行之合度者無
非天命之流行矣百祥有不集乎故小心
翼翼昭事上帝文王之所以懷多福也嚴
恭寅畏治民祇懼商宗之所以歷永年也
夫豈倖而致之歟仰惟我
皇上主敬之學心得獨邁乎百王無逸之訓操
存無間於昕夕敬
天勤民日亹亹焉夫固所以
punctuated:
何敢區區較其欽之與敬、執之與一，其孰爲在堯之德，而孰爲在我聖天子之心法也哉？先聖後聖，其揆一也，世不必同也；善繼善述，其道一也，時不必同也。故謂我皇上之敬一，得統於堯焉，同符於二祖焉，可也；謂我皇上之心學，獨得於天焉，百世以俟焉，亦可也。
抑宋儒蔡氏有言：「敬者，天之所福，百祥之所集也。」蓋人之一心有所敬畏，則精神思慮日由乎天理之中，而躬行之合度者，無非天命之流行矣。百祥有不集乎？故「小心翼翼，昭事上帝」，文王之所以懷多福也；「嚴恭寅畏」，「治民祇懼」，商宗之所以歷永年也。夫豈倖而致之歟？仰惟我皇上主敬之學，心得獨邁乎百王；無逸之訓，操存無間於昕夕。敬天勤民，日亹亹焉，夫固所以
translation_en:
…How, then, could one presume to make petty distinctions between reverent respect and reverent attentiveness, or between holding fast and unity, asking which belongs to Yao’s virtue and which to the method of cultivating the mind practiced by our sagely Son of Heaven? Earlier and later sages follow the same standard, though their ages need not be the same. Those who ably carry forward and fulfill their predecessors’ purposes follow the same Way, though their times need not be the same. Thus, one may say that our emperor’s reverence and unity inherit the tradition of Yao and accord with the Two Founding Ancestors. One may also say that our emperor’s learning of the mind is received uniquely from Heaven and can await confirmation by sages a hundred generations hence.
Furthermore, the Song Confucian scholar Cai said: “Reverence is what Heaven blesses and where the hundred auspicious blessings gather.” When a person’s mind holds something in reverence and awe, his spiritual energies and thoughts daily follow the proper course of Heaven’s principle, and all his conduct that accords with the proper standards is an unfolding of Heaven’s mandate. How could the hundred auspicious blessings fail to gather? Thus, “With care and vigilance, he illustriously served the Lord on High”: this was how King Wen received his many blessings. “Solemnly respectful and reverently apprehensive,” and “governing the people with reverent caution”: this was how the ancestral king of Shang enjoyed so many years. Could these things have come about merely by good fortune? We reverently consider that, in his learning centered on reverence, our emperor’s inward understanding uniquely surpasses that of the hundred kings. In observing the admonition against ease, he maintains this disposition without interruption, morning and evening. Revering Heaven and diligently caring for the people, he labors tirelessly each day. This, indeed, is the means by which…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
基命永固駕周軼商而與天地同悠久者也
天降景瑞曠世希覯旣昭示之矣愚也翔泳道
化之中躬睹其盛幸矣又豈能測高遠而
極淵深哉膚聞末說惟執事其進教之謹
對
第二問
馬希煃
同考試官教諭余批策士以人物一觀考古之學一
察諸生胸中錙銖而非漫然博舉而策難之也子能考
===
核詳盡品藻明當非尚友有素者能之乎
同考試官教諭陳批理學一策正以觀士子所向子
能詮次往哲旣覈且孚而景行之志溢於言外殆能闖
濂洛關閩之門而覩其奧者歟
考試官教授韓批條答明悉足占所養
考試官教授劉批評騭精覈足占尚友之志
嘗謂儒者之學學爲聖人而已論人者折
衷於聖人之道則天下無遺議矣蓋天下
之道貞于一而發明全體于聖人聖人者
punctuated:
基命永固，駕周軼商，而與天地同悠久者也。天降景瑞，曠世希覯，旣昭示之矣。愚也翔泳道化之中，躬睹其盛，幸矣！又豈能測高遠而極淵深哉？膚聞末說，惟執事其進教之。謹對。
第二問
馬希煃
同考試官教諭余批：策士以人物，一觀考古之學，一察諸生胸中錙銖，而非漫然博舉而策難之也。子能考核詳盡，品藻明當，非尚友有素者能之乎？
同考試官教諭陳批：理學一策，正以觀士子所向。子能詮次往哲，旣覈且孚，而景行之志溢於言外，殆能闖濂洛關閩之門而覩其奧者歟？
考試官教授韓批：條答明悉，足占所養。
考試官教授劉批：評騭精覈，足占尚友之志。
嘗謂儒者之學，學爲聖人而已。論人者折衷於聖人之道，則天下無遺議矣。蓋天下之道貞于一，而發明全體于聖人。聖人者
translation_en:
…secure the foundations of the heavenly mandate forever, surpass Zhou and Shang, and endure as long as Heaven and Earth. Heaven has sent down magnificent auspicious signs, seldom witnessed in many ages, and has already made this abundantly manifest. Immersed in the transforming influence of the Way, I, in my ignorance, am fortunate to witness this flourishing age in person! Yet how could I fathom its lofty reach or plumb its profound depths? These are superficial observations and insignificant explanations; I ask you, honored examiners, to instruct me further. Respectfully submitted in reply.
Second Question
Ma Xikui
Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor: “In examining candidates through questions about historical figures, our purposes are to observe their learning in the study of antiquity and to discern the fine measures by which they weigh matters in their minds. We do not indiscriminately cite a wide range of examples merely to pose difficult questions. Your examination of the evidence is thorough, and your appraisals are clear and fitting. Could anyone achieve this without long practice in taking the worthy of antiquity as friends?”
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “This policy question on the Learning of Principle is intended precisely to reveal the direction of candidates’ aspirations. You have arranged and assessed the philosophers of the past both rigorously and convincingly, while your aspiration to emulate their lofty conduct shines through beyond your words. Perhaps you have succeeded in peering through the gates of the traditions of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min and glimpsing their deepest mysteries?”
Comment by Examiner Han, Professor: “The answers to each point are clear and comprehensive, sufficiently revealing the cultivation you have attained.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “The appraisals are perceptive and exact, sufficiently revealing your aspiration to take the worthy of antiquity as friends.”
I have often said that the learning of a Confucian consists solely in learning to become a sage. If those who assess people take the Way of the sages as their standard, no grounds for dispute will remain anywhere under Heaven. For the Way throughout the world is grounded in unity, and its entirety is made manifest in the sages. The sages are…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣西鄉試錄
text:
道學之宗斯文之的也儒者學道而以聖
人爲準則明之於心行之於身措之於事
業無非道者斯無愧於儒矣否則卽事功
著作表見一時抑其細焉而已許魯齋曰
傳記中人才傑然可觀以道理觀之只是
偏才聖人則圓融渾全百理皆具知此則
可以論古今之人物矣執事發策而以
國朝理學名臣爲問愚也學未通方何足以
尚論前哲請言其槩而就正焉可乎古人
===
===
有言曰太上立德其次立功其次立言蓋
脩已者舍是無以成名觀人者舍是無以
論世故三者皆不朽之具而亦權衡人物
之則也夫士君子之生于人國也或顯或
晦或出或處皆謂之臣或勳烈可紀或制
作可稱或文章可傳皆謂之名臣臣以名
名亦可以不朽于後世而復有所謂理學
云者自其有得於聖人之學者言之也聖
人之學心學也蘊之而爲天德發之而爲
punctuated:
道學之宗，斯文之的也。儒者學道而以聖人爲準，則明之於心，行之於身，措之於事業，無非道者，斯無愧於儒矣。否則，卽事功著作表見一時，抑其細焉而已。許魯齋曰：「傳記中人才傑然可觀，以道理觀之，只是偏才。聖人則圓融渾全，百理皆具。」知此，則可以論古今之人物矣。執事發策，而以國朝理學名臣爲問，愚也學未通方，何足以尚論前哲？請言其槩而就正焉，可乎？
